recommendation: Do NOT promote static stride-3+ROI. The compute win is real (−67% invocations, −72.7% inference) but it moves failures EARLIER in the cascade on 2/3 dev cases via tracker/selection starvation, not detection quality. For Wave B, integrate an ADAPTIVE two-pass detector policy in analyzeVideo.ts runPaddleStage (the only required TS change; detect_paddle.py already supports --stride/--roi): (1) scan pass at stride 3 + target ROI over detectSpan±250ms, ROI derived from the SEEDED target track's torso union over the event-gated span (not the largest-torso proxy) and derived over the event-gated span only — over the full window the ROI degenerates to the full frame (measured on wm-volley-02); (2) densification pass at stride 1 over selected-event peak ±450ms (the contact scope), appended into the same paddle-dets.json before tracking — this directly re-feeds the two measured failure points (contact-zone track death, selection margin) while keeping most savings since the contact scope is ~25-35% of the detect span on these cases; (3) full-frame/stride-1 FALLBACK triggers: target identity uncertain (no seed and selection confidence low, or targetCoverage < 0.5), ROI area > ~0.9 of frame (ROI no-op), torso union touching an ROI edge mid-span (motion exceeds crop), paddle stage returns untracked/ambiguous or windowCoverage < 0.3, or contact paddleConfirmed=false — re-run dense and re-track before shipping the paddle-unavailable answer; (4) flag design: --paddle-stride N (default 1), --paddle-roi auto|x0,y0,x1,y1|off, wired into the runPaddleStage execFileSync argv; CRITICAL: the reuse gate must also compare detector.stride/roiNorm in the existing file against the requested config — today it only checks window coverage, so a stride-3 file is silently reused for a stride-1 request (this is what made the sandbox swap work, and it is also a footgun); (5) re-validate the adaptive policy full-pipeline on dev before any held-out run, and only then regenerate held-out ONCE.
risks: n=3 dev cases, 23 visible paddle labels, 3 gold events — per-stage flips of a single case dominate rates; treat deltas as directional forensics, not stable estimates
rally2 baseline was already marginal (selection margin 1.2527 vs 1.25 gate): the PADDLE regression there is gate-edge sensitivity, and any detector nondeterminism on mps could flip it run-to-run

the ROI derivation in roi_keyframe_grid.py uses the largest-torso person as 'target' proxy, not the seeded target track — on far-player or multi-player footage a production ROI from the wrong person would crop out the real paddle; must derive from the seeded identity

wm-volley-02 ROI computed over the full detector window degenerates to [0,0,1,1]; ROI is only meaningful when derived from the event-gated span — an integration that derives it from the padded window silently loses the quality lever

S0 under the waterfall convention (±40ms) structurally penalizes stride 3 (inter-frame gap 100-120ms); quality conclusions here rest on the grid convention and on downstream stages, and the downstream regressions are the binding constraint
timing measured on one mps laptop with ~2x day-to-day ms/frame variance vs recorded canonicals; relative deltas (same-day back-to-back) are trustworthy, absolute seconds are not
held-out cases (wm-dink-01, afn-vic-rally1) and the shadow split were not touched; the adaptive Wave B policy must be re-validated on dev first, then held-out exactly once
ball-stage coupling: when paddle goes untracked, ball gating loosens and can flip untracked→tracked (measured on rally2) — cascade accounting should treat that flip as an artifact, not an improvement
